title: Merge Intervals
statement: Given an array of intervals where `intervals[i] = [start, end]`, merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

examples.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they merge into [1,6].
Intervals touching at an endpoint are considered overlapping.

optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time dominated by the sort, O(n) space for the output.
rubric: Sorts by start before scanning. Attempting to merge unsorted intervals is the classic wrong turn.
Extends the last interval with Math.max rather than blindly taking the current end — a fully contained interval must not shrink the result.
Can state why the complexity is O(n log n) and not O(n).
followUps: What if the intervals arrived as a stream and you had to keep a running merge?
Insert one new interval into an already-merged list in O(n).
What is the maximum number of intervals overlapping at any point in time?
